title.narrative: Cambodia Australia Partnership for Resilient Economic Development (CAPRED)

description.narrative: CAPRED is Australia's flagship bilateral economic development program in Cambodia focusing on supporting economic recovery and boosting resilience. CAPRED’s goal is to ensure Cambodia has sustainable, resilient and inclusive economic growth and development. The program objective is that Cambodian women and men equally benefit from increased access to, or increased participation in, environmentally sustainable, economically resilient and inclusive economic growth.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: CAPRED helped launch a new rice variety, Champei Sar 70, building on nine years of Australian support to the agricultural sector. The new variety is more drought & flood resilient and can be grown 2-3 times a year, raising annual production and incomes for farmers. CAPRED supported the increased uptake of the new variety by distributing rice seeds to provincial departments of agriculture, the Cambodian Rice Federation, agriculture cooperatives and farmers. It also published a video and manual for producers. CAPRED support helped ensure broad public awareness and uptake of this variety.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: CAPRED is supporting Cambodia to increase its access to climate finance through support to the Cambodia Climate Financing Facility (CCFF). Through Green Climate Fund financing, the CCFF will provide long-term concessional financing to private sector projects in climate adaptation and mitigation, focusing on water management, energy efficiency and renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and transport. CAPRED is working with the local implementing bank to establish the operating framework and providing capacity building to ensure the CCFF becomes operational by mid-2025.

CAPRED is supporting the CNAI Accelerator Program for emerging women entrepreneurs. This activity is providing valuable insights to entrepreneurs regarding business operations, financial management, and HR management with a focus on Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI). This support is assisting entrepreneurs to scale their operations and enhance their growth potential, as well as to overcome critical challenges, expand their market reach, and foster a more inclusive and dynamic entrepreneurial ecosystem in Cambodia.

CAPRED is supporting the Ministry of Mines and Energy (MME) and Electricity du Cambodge (EDC) on Cambodia’s clean energy transition, including collaborating with relevant institutions to develop a suitable energy forecast system for Cambodia. Additionally, the program is also supporting a Provincial Investment Plan study which will create a commercial piped water supply database to guide regulatory boundaries, sector financing, and integrated water management.

CAPRED provided fifteen women entrepreneurs with business development services through two visits to Australia. The first provided six female entrepreneurs with leadership training to improve the performance of their business, increase their market access, and to strengthen their ability to compete in the marketplace. The second tour connected nine female-led Cambodian agri-food enterprises to investors and buyers in Australia. These entrepreneurs gained experience and first-hand knowledge of Australian markets and best practice, and several have since received expressions of interest from Australian companies to buy their products and/or invest in their businesses.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: CAPRED supported the Government’s objective to establish an Agri-food Industrial Park (AIP) to increase agro-processing and stimulate Cambodia’s economic growth. With CAPRED policy and technical assistance, the Government has established an AIP governance structure, including secretariat and leadership committee, strengthened regulatory capacity, and built linkages between Cambodian and Australian agencies and industrial park operators.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Cambodia’s agri-food sector faces challenges in export competitiveness due to limited product quality, weak market access and low investment in processing. Through the Cambodia Australia Partnership for Resilient Economic Development (CAPRED), Australia supported 28 market actors in 2024-25 to strengthen supply chains and expand access to domestic and international markets. Twelve SMEs received tailored support to improve product quality and packaging while promoting innovation and competitiveness. Participation of eight market actors was supported through an export readiness program, including a trade mission to Europe to engage with buyers and ensure compliance with international export standards. Early results include a rice exporter securing a contract to supply 800 tons annually to Australia, worth over AUD 1.2 million. A Cambodian-Australian investor committed AUD 500,000 to expand cashew processing. These initiatives have created over 10 new rural jobs, with local staff collectively earning more than AUD 20,000 annually, contributing to inclusive economic growth and more resilient agri-food value chains.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Efforts to strengthen governance and inclusive practices are a key priority for Cambodian institutions as they work to become more responsive to diverse community needs. In 2024-25, through CAPRED, Australia supported 39 organisations to strengthen governance by promoting inclusion and accountability. CAPRED provided four government institutions (Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology & Innovation, Office of the Council of Ministers, Phnom Penh Water Supply Authority and Siem Reap Waterworks) with targeted assistance around monitoring and evaluation systems and water law dissemination. ‍ Four civil society organisations (Cambodia Rice Federation, Cambodia Water Supply Association, SAORI Handweaving, and Cambodia Development Resource Institute (CDRI)) improved governance structures with support for inclusive representation and internal systems. ‍ Fifty private sector organisations at regional, national and local levels received assistance to apply Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards, conduct energy audits and adopt inclusive business practices. Several SMEs adopted workplace harassment policies and grievance procedures, integrating them into human resource systems. They also developed tailored staff training tools to foster safer, more inclusive workplaces. For example, Green Living, a growing cashew company, is using these tools to support responsible employment as it scales operations. These tools help improve team dynamics, boost staff retention, and enhance inclusivity.

People with disabilities in Cambodia face systemic barriers to entrepreneurship, including a lack of tailored business support, limited access to networks and exclusion from mainstream economic development programs. CAPRED’s inclusive and tailored business support strengthened market readiness, promoted economic empowerment for people with disabilities and laid the groundwork for sustainable enterprise growth. Through the Mekong Inclusive Ventures (MIV) incubator, CAPRED launched Cambodia’s first tailored business incubation program for disability-led and inclusive SMEs. Seven businesses completed the program throughout 2024-25. A key component of the program was a financial literacy session that addressed common capacity gaps. Following the financial literacy session, over 80 per cent of incubator participants reported greater confidence in using financial data to inform business decisions. Several SMEs improved pricing, budgeting and investment planning—early signs of stronger resilience. In parallel, CAPRED also supported SAORI Handweaving, which operates as both a non-government organisation and a social enterprise employing people with disabilities, to strengthen its structure and market readiness through tailored support in operations, branding and strategy. SAORI increased production capacity from 20 units per year to 20 per month and expanded employment opportunities for women with disabilities, directly boosting their incomes and skills development.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Rural communities in Cambodia, especially, women and persons with disabilities, face persistent barriers to accessing safe, reliable drinking water due to low infrastructure investment and limited service coverage. Through CAPRED, Australia enabled 7,607 people, including 5,071 women and 19 persons with disabilities, to gain access to safely managed drinking water in 2024-25. This was achieved through an adapted Viability Gap Financing model, a co-funding initiative with private operators to expand their services to remote areas. The program partnered with four private water operators in three districts of Takeo and Kampong Thom to support piped, treated water connections across nine communes. A targeted AUD 53 subsidy per connection was provided for households with persons with disabilities, alongside technical assistance to strengthen service delivery. Household-level water meters improved service accountability and encouraged responsible water use, while significantly reducing the time, especially for women, spent collecting water. By supporting infrastructure in areas previously considered commercially unviable, Australia contributed to more inclusive and climate-resilient rural development. The initiative demonstrated a replicable model for public-private collaboration in water service delivery, and its lessons are informing the development of Cambodia’s Clean Water Development Fund—a key step toward water equity and sustainability.

Women entrepreneurs in Cambodia continue to face barriers to growing their businesses, including limited access to finance, business development services and investor networks. In 2024-25, through CAPRED, Australia supported 33 women entrepreneurs with targeted financial and business development assistance delivered through the CNai Accelerator and Mekong Inclusive Ventures (MIV) incubators. ‍ CNai Accelerator provided sixteen women-led businesses with structured training, mentoring, pitch preparation and exposure to potential investors. Nine additional women-led SMEs, including eight led by women with disabilities, were supported through MIV with tailored incubation, technical support and catalytic grant funding. ‍ One example is CamAgro-Food, a food producer that secured AUD 45,454 in funding through CNai. By transforming surplus produce into high-quality, value-added products, CamAgro-Food increased its profits five-fold. "After joining the CNai program, I noticed two developments: the first is personal development, and the second is business development," said Soukhim, founder of CamAgro-Food. ‍ The program led to the creation of 14 new jobs, eight filled by women. Staff earned over AUD 23,182 in additional income, while participating businesses reported improvements in branding, new retail partnerships, and greater financial literacy and business confidence. Overall, the program mobilised AUD 3.6 million in private investment, boosting the growth potential of women-led enterprises.
